deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues Gauss's study of the lemniscatic function P (next page: 'Es sei Pφ = φ − φ^5/60 + &c.'; previous page: theta-type expansions of P(a+bi)ϖ). Here P is written as a series in x. The verification below shows that P coincides with the Weierstrass sigma function for g2 = 4, g3 = 0.

(1) Top row. Gauss lists the coefficients c_1..c_5 of
  log(P(x)/x) = Σ_k c_k x^{4k}:
  c1 = −1/(4·3·5) = −1/60
  c2 = −1/(8·3·25·7) = −1/4200
  c3 = −1/(2·9·125·11·13) = −1/321750
  c4 = −1/(16·9·625·13·17) = −1/19890000
  c5 = −1/(2·9·15625·13·17·19) = −1/1180968750
[Mine:] These equal −b_k/(4k(4k−1)), where ℘(x) = x^{-2} + Σ b_k x^{4k−2} is the lemniscatic ℘ with g2 = 4. Then b1 = 1/5, b2 = 1/75, b3 = 2/4875, b4 = 1/82875, b5 = 2/6215625, since (log σ)'' = −℘.

(2) 'Coeff. x^13 in P'. Write P = x·exp(Σ c_k x^{4k}). The coefficient of x^13 is a sum over the partitions 3, 2+1, 1+1+1 of 3, with multinomial weights (1/6 for 1.1.1):
  c3 + c1c2 + c1^3/6 = −1/(2·9·125·11·13) + 1/(32·9·125·7) − 1/(128·81·125).
Over the common denominator 128·81·125·7·11·13 the numerators are −4032 + 5148 − 1001 = 115 (a first −576 is struck out). This gives
  +23/(128·81·25·7·11·13) = 552/13!.
The marginal 143, 429, 858 are scratch work.

(3) 'Coeff. von x^21 in P'. Partitions of 5, each term with its correct multinomial weight:
  5: −1/(2·9·15625·13·17·19)
  4.1: +1/(64·27·3125·13·17)
  3.2: +1/(16·27·3125·7·11·13)
  3.1.1 (c3c1²/2): −1/(64·81·3125·11·13), with 128 corrected to 64
  2.2.1 (c2²c1/2): −1/(512·27·3125·49)
  2.1.1.1 (c2c1³/6): +1/(1024·243·3125·7)
  1^5 (c1^5/120): −1/(8192·729·15625)
Pairwise combinations:
  5 + 4.1 = −1/(64·27·15625·13·17·19)
  3.2 + 3.1.1 = +1/(64·81·625·7·11·13)
Next he factors out the common factor 64·27·625 ('also jetzt gemeinschaftl.'). The remaining reciprocals are 25·13·17·19, 3·7·11·13, 8·5·49, 16·9·5·7 and 128·27·25. Over D = 128·27·25·49·11·13·17·19 the numerators are
  −1862784, +65116800, −99768240, +38798760, −2263261.
Partial sums: +63254016, −60969480, +2284536, and finally +21275 = 25·851 = 25·23·37. Hence the coefficient is
  +23·37/(8192·729·625·49·11·13·17·19).

(4) Factorials (Πn = n!) in prime-factored form:
  Π8 = 2^7·3^2·5·7
  Π11 = 2^8·3^4·5^2·7·11
  Π14 = 2^11·3^5·5^2·7^2·11·13
  Π17 = 2^15·3^6·5^3·7^2·11·13·17
  Π21 = 2^18·3^9·5^4·7^3·11·13·17·19
Therefore Coeff(x^21) = 32·27·7·23·37/Π21 = 5146848/21!. The marginal 720·7·8 = 8!/… and 2187 = 3^7 are scratch work for these.

[Mine:] In Weierstrass's normalisation σ = Σ a_{m,n}(g2/2)^m(2g3)^n z^{4m+6n+1}/(4m+6n+1)!, this reads 552 = 69·2^3 and 5146848 = 160839·2^5. These are the known a_{3,0} = 69 and a_{5,0} = 160839. So P is exactly the lemniscatic sigma function, and Gauss is computing its Taylor coefficients up to x^21, presumably to check numerically against the theta-series representation on the adjacent pages.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every partition term, every partial sum (63254016, −60969480, 2284536, 21275), the factorization 21275 = 25·23·37, and all factorial factorizations check out.
Self-corrections visible on the page: 128 → 64 in the 3.1.1 term (64 is correct); a struck −576 before −4032 in the x^13 computation; 49 inserted in the common denominator 128·27·25·49·11·13·17·19.

results.modern_name: Power series of the Weierstrass sigma function for the lemniscatic lattice (g2=4, g3=0); coefficients a_{3,0}=69, a_{5,0}=160839 of Weierstrass's recursion
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (sigma function and its coefficient recursion, 1882); the lemniscatic P function itself is known from Gauss's Nachlass (Werke III)

results.what: Exponentiating a power series via a sum over partitions with weights 1/∏(multiplicity)!
results.modern_name: Exponential formula / Faà di Bruno-type expansion of exp of a series
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler era; Faà di Bruno 1855 for the general formula)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic P (the sigma function for g2=4) and its series are documented in his Nachlass. This page is a careful, correct computation of high-order coefficients (up to x^21) by the log-series and partition method. The numbers agree with Weierstrass's later table, but this is computational detail rather than a new result.

checkable.sympy: z=symbols('z'); c=[Rational(-1,60),Rational(-1,4200),Rational(-1,321750),Rational(-1,19890000),Rational(-1,1180968750)]; s=series(z*exp(sum(c[k]*z**(4*k+4) for k in range(5))),z,0,23).removeO(); [s.coeff(z,13)*factorial(13), s.coeff(z,21)*factorial(21)]
checkable.asserts: Coefficients of z^13 and z^21 times the factorials equal [552, 5146848]
Final form of the x^21 coefficient over 21!
Gauss's factorizations of Π8, Π11, Π14, Π17, Π21
The c_k equal −b_k/(4k(4k−1)) from the Laurent coefficients of the lemniscatic ℘ (g2=4), i.e. P is the sigma function
